Inspect fitted estimates and interpretation status

Source: R/api-methods.R
summary.mfrm_fit.Rd

Summarize a fitted model without changing its estimates. The default returns fit-only tables; read s$decision after s <- summary(fit) for interpretation limits and next actions. Individual estimates are available separately through as.data.frame(fit).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_fit'
summary(
  object,
  digits = 3,
  top_n = 5,
  ...,
  profile = c("fit", "facets", "reporting"),
  detail = NULL,
  diagnostics = NULL,
  compute = c("auto", "never"),
  include_person = FALSE,
  comparison_review = NULL
)

Arguments

object

Output from fit_mfrm().

digits

Number of digits for printed numeric values.

top_n

Number of extreme facet/person rows shown in summaries.

...

Reserved for generic compatibility. The workflow arguments that follow ... must be supplied by name.

profile

Summary profile. "fit" preserves the lightweight fit-only contract and does not compute diagnostics. "facets" adds a comprehensive measurement review using familiar FACETS-style section organization; it does not require FACETS knowledge or software. "reporting" adds the reporting-oriented results profile.

detail

Printed detail. When NULL (the default), the lightweight "fit" profile retains the legacy "full" print while expanded profiles use "brief". Neither mode prints person identifiers unless include_person = TRUE; "brief" also reduces the number of fit-level sections shown in the console.

diagnostics

Optional matching output from diagnose_mfrm(). It is reused by the "facets" and "reporting" profiles without recomputation.

compute

Diagnostic computation policy for the expanded profiles. "auto" computes diagnostics once when they were not supplied; "never" returns the available fit-only portions and marks every requested dependent section as "not_computed". The "fit" profile never computes diagnostics.

include_person

Logical. Whether person identifiers may be printed in extreme-person tables and requested by the fit-pathway route. The default is FALSE for privacy-safe console output.

comparison_review

Optional prospective interaction review from describe_mfrm_data(). Explicitly requests fitted contrasts and retained- point numerical checks through interaction_effect_table(), saved as $interaction_comparisons. It does not fit a model or supply intervals.

Value

A summary.mfrm_fit list. Components are grouped below by purpose; model-specific components are populated only where supported.

Interpretation and availability

  • decision: interpretation, FormalInference, Why and NextAction, combining source-fit readiness with supplied precision evidence. "No" can mean that precision has not been assessed, rather than that point estimation failed. "Yes" is conditional on the fitted model and checked method; it does not establish model adequacy or finite-sample coverage.

  • status, readiness, data_review: compact status, separate workflow states and their connectivity/category-support evidence. InferenceReady is a compatibility indicator for stored FitReadiness = "ready"; numerical convergence cannot override data, estimability or boundary issues.

  • key_warnings, notes, next_actions: issues and follow-up calls. caveats retains the detailed score-support and population-design rows, including omissions or unstable residual variance where recorded.

  • section_status: availability, including requested but not_computed sections. An unassessed check is not a passed check.

Estimates and model settings

  • overview: counts, likelihood, information criteria and convergence. MMLEngineUsed, IterationsBasis and ConvergenceBasis identify the algorithm and stopping record. See compare_mfrm() and the information-criterion section of fit_mfrm_technical_details for eligibility, MML denominators based on Persons and quadrature requirements before ranking models.

  • person_overview, facet_overview, targeting: distributions and Person-versus-facet targeting. For the meaning and direction of individual Estimate values, see as.data.frame.mfrm_fit(). A blocked source fit's extreme MML EAPs are excluded from aggregate Person/targeting summaries but retained in the extreme tables; counts, exclusions and estimate use are reported.

  • person_high, person_low, facet_extremes: extreme estimates; Person identifiers are printed only with include_person = TRUE.

  • step_overview: spread and monotonicity by PCM/GPCM StepFacet ladder, or the common RSM ladder.

  • settings_overview: identification, category and numerical settings. CenteringScope distinguishes whole-facet and remainder centering from NoncenterFacet. CategoryPolicy is the declared choice; ScoreRecoded records actual value changes. An unchanged score map does not identify the policy. Missing historical metadata retain legacy centering and "not_recorded"/NA category fields. Regenerate the summary from its fit to obtain new fields; reading an old summary does not update stored results.

  • population_overview, population_coefficients, population_design, population_coding: population basis/variance/omissions, active regression coefficients, design checks, and categorical levels/contrasts needed when scoring new Persons.

  • interaction_overview: fitted interactions. interaction_comparisons appears only when requested through comparison_review, preserving unavailable contrasts, the review and numerical checks without new fitting.

Numerical and boundary evidence

  • numerical_review: optimization, curvature, starting-value, integration and reproducible-refit checks with next actions; does not change readiness.

  • starting_values, starting_value_notes: all attempted starts, selection, failures and cautions after fit_mfrm(mml_starts = ...). These concern numerical sensitivity, not sampling uncertainty.

  • facet_support_boundaries: observed boundary-constant facet levels; these alone do not prove infinite MLEs. facet_recession_review records certified JML additive recession directions, their scope and completeness. Joint rows are relative directions under the fitted constraints.

  • slope_overview: GPCM slope-owner and parameter-status summary. Min, Max and GeometricMean use primary estimates; Optimizer* fields retain numerical iterates where primary estimates are unavailable. An identification constraint does not establish precision.

  • inference_evidence: GPCM MML stationarity, local rank, information, slope-boundary screening and final decision. Local evidence does not override an inconclusive boundary audit.

  • point_estimation: for two-family GPCM and supported endpoint reductions, the point-estimate status and separate integration, local-maximum and limited boundary reviews. This does not qualify SEs or intervals. Older fits are labelled unreviewed

  • point_targets, step_targets, point_limit, and optional category_map: target status, refit counts and original score labels for supported GPCM limiting-likelihood estimates; see mfrmr_gpcm_scope for the distinction between deliberately skipped optimization, numerical failure and available limiting estimates

  • rating_support, rating_crossings, rating_categories, rating_support_notes: two-family per-level persons, rating rows, per-person exposure, marginal crossings and category counts. DataBasis separates full-model and limiting-fit data. Counts do not qualify precision

Preparation and reporting

  • row_retention, preparation_notes: retained rows and preparation records.

  • attached_diagnostics, attached_diagnostics_cols: whether diagnostics were attached to the fit, and which columns were attached to Person rows.

  • reporting_map, required_visual: companion tables and ordered Wright-map/ fit-pathway routes for reporting. Figure availability does not qualify intervals.

  • provenance, analysis: profile, diagnostic source, computation policy and compact fit/results indexes. results is the reused mfrm_results() object for expanded profiles, or NULL for the default fit-only profile.

  • digits: numeric print precision. Printing does not refit or change the stored tables.

Details

Keep the fitted object for further analysis. s <- summary(fit) saves tables; print s or select a component with $. Start with s$decision, then s$person_overview and s$facet_overview. These describe distributions of estimates; use as.data.frame(fit) for individual Person and facet-level rows. Centered facet means can be zero by constraint, so compare levels or their spread rather than interpreting the mean as an empirical finding.

The default profile = "fit" does not compute diagnostics. For an ordinary RSM/PCM precision review, pass matching diagnostics = diagnose_mfrm(fit); reuse existing diagnostics when available. Read decision$Why together with the parameter-specific status; the Value section explains the decision fields.

Expanded profiles use FACETS-style organization without running FACETS or claiming numerical equivalence. Reuse their $results and $results$diagnostics for further reporting.

Corrected JML

Corrected JML returns a separate summary of saved tables, numerical attempts, correction order and RootSE interpretation. All profiles use that same saved summary without ordinary diagnostics. include_person = TRUE adds conditional Person profiles without Person SEs. See fit_mfrm_technical_details; the Value section describes uncorrected fits.

See also

fit_mfrm(), diagnose_mfrm()

Examples

library(mfrmr)

# Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit

# Save the summary, then display its tables
results <- summary(fit)
results$person_overview # One row summarizing person ability estimates
#> # A tibble: 1 × 11
#>   Persons DistributionN ReviewExcludedExtremeE…¹ EstimateUse   Mean    SD Median
#>     <int>         <int>                    <int> <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1      48            48                        0 source_fit… -0.155 0.824 -0.208
#> # ℹ abbreviated name: ¹​ReviewExcludedExtremeEAPs
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: Min <dbl>, Max <dbl>, Span <dbl>, MeanPosteriorSD <dbl>
results$facet_overview  # One row per facet: number of levels, mean, SD, range
#> # A tibble: 2 × 7
#>   Facet     Levels MeanEstimate SDEstimate MinEstimate MaxEstimate  Span
#>   <chr>      <int>        <dbl>      <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 Criterion      3     4.62e-18      0.302      -0.344       0.224 0.568
#> 2 Rater          6     0             0.399      -0.606       0.412 1.02 

# Check the interpretation status and recommended next step
results$decision
#>                                                           Interpretation
#> 1 Fit-readiness requirements satisfied; formal precision review required
#>   FormalInference FitReadiness
#> 1              No        ready
#>                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      Why
#> 1 Formal precision support has not been evaluated. These checks assess numerical readiness and the requested precision method under the specified model; they do not establish model adequacy or finite-sample coverage for this design.
#>                                                                                                                                                   NextAction
#> 1 Run `diagnose_mfrm()` and pass its result as `diagnostics =` to evaluate formal precision support; fit readiness alone is not a formal-inference decision.

# Extract estimates and select the rows to display
estimates <- as.data.frame(fit)
head(subset(estimates, Facet == "Person")) # First six persons
#>    Facet Level    Estimate Extreme
#> 1 Person  P001  0.28429588    none
#> 2 Person  P002  0.66118004    none
#> 3 Person  P003  0.02177773    none
#> 4 Person  P004  0.22410785    none
#> 5 Person  P005 -0.17496065    none
#> 6 Person  P006  0.67681003    none
subset(estimates, Facet == "Rater")       # All raters
#>    Facet Level   Estimate Extreme
#> 49 Rater   R01 -0.6059776    <NA>
#> 50 Rater   R02 -0.3820356    <NA>
#> 51 Rater   R03  0.2120388    <NA>
#> 52 Rater   R04  0.1799462    <NA>
#> 53 Rater   R05  0.1842365    <NA>
#> 54 Rater   R06  0.4117917    <NA>
subset(estimates, Facet == "Criterion")   # All criteria
#>        Facet        Level   Estimate Extreme
#> 55 Criterion      Content -0.3441471    <NA>
#> 56 Criterion     Language  0.1204520    <NA>
#> 57 Criterion Organization  0.2236950    <NA>
